reachabilityVerdict.interpretation: Two distinct Akamai Bot Manager outcomes per UA: (1) production default Chrome 120 UA => hard 403 EdgeSuite Access-Denied on EVERY product surface (/home, /l/, /p/) on the FIRST single GET. (2) iPhone Safari 17 UA => HTTP 200 but body is the Akamai behavioral-challenge interstitial (~2KB sec-if-cpt-container + akam-sw.js service-worker installer), which carries ZERO products. A 200-status-but-challenge-body is a SOFT block: extractCatalogProducts/extractProducts would return 0 from it, and the >5KB-static-HTML Playwright auto-fallback would NOT even fire (challenge body is <5KB). No product surface (HTML SSR or challenge-passing) is reachable for the crawler from this IP under any production UA.
reachabilityVerdict.noEscalationNote: Statuses were stable across the 8 spaced probes (clean surfaces 200 real-content; product surfaces 403 or 200-challenge). No 429, no rate-limit headers, no escalating ban. The block is policy/fingerprint-based (per-UA + TLS/JA3 + behavioral), not request-rate-based, so a slower walk does NOT help. Did NOT run the heavy-probe rapid burst (operator instruction).

r1ContradictionSettled.answer: BOTH observations were correct for their UA. The 2026-06-02 R1 ran a single-UA Chrome 120 gentle GET => 403 everywhere (reproduced exactly: /home 403/372B, /l/firearms 403/382B). The B6 batch (2026-05-23) used Safari 17 macOS with PRE-WARMED Akamai geo cookies and got page-1 SSR 200 (56KB /home, 433KB /l/firearms) but page-2 (?page=N&firstResult=M) re-403. Net: page-1 SSR is reachable ONLY with a non-Chrome UA AND pre-warmed Akamai cookies; even then it renders products client-side (0 in static HTML) and pagination re-403s. With a cold session under any production UA (no cookie pre-warm), today's result is 403 (Chrome) or behavioral-challenge interstitial (iPhone). The crawler cannot obtain products either way.
r1ContradictionSettled.postureDifference: R1's 'all 403' vs B6's 'page-1 200' is explained entirely by UA + cookie-pre-warm posture, NOT by Akamai hardening over time. The Akamai block was present and effective in both windows. Today: clean infra surfaces (robots+sitemap) still 200 (B6 + today agree); product surfaces still blocked (B6 + today agree). No access change.
